subject.title: Discord leaks internal tool-call traces (NO_REPLY, commentary, to=functions) to channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord-specific or shared outbound guard for envelope-shaped internal traces such as to=functions.*, recipient_name, parameters, and short tool-argument JSON, and what false-positive boundary should that guard enforce?
rationale: The remaining behavior is security-sensitive channel output, but the safe fix boundary is not purely mechanical because aggressive filtering can suppress legitimate Discord markdown, code fences, or JSON examples.

options.title: Approve Narrow Sanitizer Boundary
options.body: Define a focused shared or Discord sanitizer for internal envelope-shaped traces, require code-fence/JSON false-positive tests, and keep the broader explicit-send policy separate.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Delivery Policy
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/25592 the canonical owner and preserve this issue's Discord envelope checklist there before closing this one later.

options.title: Require Live Repro First
options.body: Keep implementation paused until a maintainer or reporter provides a fresh redacted Discord reproduction for the remaining envelope variants.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Sanitizer Boundary
recommendation.body: Define a focused shared or Discord sanitizer for internal envelope-shaped traces, require code-fence/JSON false-positive tests, and keep the broader explicit-send policy separate.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans security/product policy and current-main delivery behavior, and this account is the strongest available maintainer-routing signal in the inspected history.
